directlyComparableWhen: the payloadSizes iterator is present and known to be aligned one-to-one with the PacketEntities entry
the entry action actually consumed its payload region between afterCommand and afterAction
afterCommand is the intended start of the payload span for that command/action path
afterAction was recorded after the same action span without early fail-closed termination
the command path has no separately-accounted reads that should be excluded from payloadBits
notComparableWhen: the parser fails closed before applying or extracting the payload
payloadBits is null or the payload-size iterator is unavailable
the entry is LEAVE or DELETE and local handler records payloadBits as 0
the entry uses a filtered skip path whose cursor movement intentionally relies on payloadBits rather than independent extraction
iterator alignment, command semantics, or payload span semantics are under investigation
conditionalOrWeakWhen: previous neighboring entries compare cleanly but one entry diverges
read counts are monotonic and within entityData but the action span exceeds payloadBits
nearby offset alternatives exist but are only compact candidates
no raw payload/entityData inspection is permitted

reviewConclusion: Task 147's comparison is a useful compact diagnostic signal only under stated conditions; it should not be treated as a primary parser bug proof or a skip/recovery contract.
